question: Why is cefazolin short, and what do we do?

steps.title: Our stock in three hospitals
steps.purpose: Read on-hand stock and 28-day use where each hospital keeps it.
steps.finding: 11 stock lines across 3 hospitals, 4 presentations, in units of use.

steps.title: Where our supply is made

steps.finding: Not on FDA's current shortage list.

steps.finding: 15 labelers make it in this form.

steps.title: What FDA found at those plants
steps.purpose: Read every FDA drug inspection, warning letter, import alert and recall for these plants.
steps.finding: 20 inspections (1 OAI at our plants), 1 compliance actions, 0 import-alert listings, 1 recalls.

steps.title: What FDA wrote at the OAI inspections
steps.purpose: Read the Form 483 observations recorded at those inspections.

steps.title: What our P&T committee already approved
steps.purpose: Read Corvale General's approved interchanges for these items.

steps.purpose: Run the semantic layer's key rules (NDC and unit of use) over each hospital's stock, and name the rows they reject.
steps.finding: 11 stock rows across the system fail the NDC rule; 0 of them are this drug. Every row is in a shared unit of use.

steps.title: What we decided last time
steps.purpose: Recall past decisions on this drug from H-MEM, with who approved them.
steps.finding: No past decisions on this drug.

sentences.text: FDA's records show cefazolin sodium is not on the current shortage list as of 2026-10-21; an earlier shortage was first posted 2018-11-30 and is resolved.

FDA inspected the Hikma Farmaceutica (Portugal) S.A. plant (FEI 3002807173) multiple times, including an OAI classification on 2014-03-28 and a Warning Letter on 2014-10-21, with the most recent VAI on 2023-04-21.
The 2018-11-30 shortage posting came 962 days after a VAI inspection ended 2016-04-12 at that plant.
A later VAI inspection ended 2020-03-06, 462 days after the 2018-11-30 posting.
Corvale East holds 128 units of the 2 g/50 mL presentation at 14.4 per day (8.9 days on hand) and Corvale General holds 279 units at 16.1 per day (17.3 days on hand).
The rule-based best option is to transfer 53 units of 2 g/50 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East, which would leave Corvale General with 14 days and bring Corvale East to 13 days.
